clue.text: Carry outside each cold bun

indicators.note: one word standing outside others means it wraps around them, so the first word goes round the rest

blocks.note: to carry something away is to take it
the standard abbreviation for each
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a cold bun out of a café for every person in the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry outside' reads as taking food out, but it tells you the word for carry goes round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a sweet yeasted roll, often with currants, usually served toasted and buttered.

clue.text: Easily charm tribe that'll exchange shells

indicators.note: the following letters are said to go easily into a new order, rearranged without effort

blocks.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A tribe that is easily charmed, perhaps by beads and trinkets offered in trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange shells' sounds like barter in cowries, which fits the tribe picture; in fact it describes a crustacean moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean lives in borrowed empty mollusc homes and swaps into a bigger one as it grows.

clue.text: Slasher and boss (at time of writing) -  foxtrot off!

indicators.note: telling a letter to be off means it is sent away and dropped from the word

blocks.note: the US president when this appeared, Donald Trump, is a convicted criminal
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A rant about a cost-cutting tycoon and his president, ending in a barely disguised swear word.
explanation.walkthrough: FELON minus F gives ELON. The clue dates from 2025, when the convicted president Trump was in office and Elon Musk led his DOGE spending cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Elon Musk headed the Department of Government Efficiency, famous for cutting federal jobs and budgets with a chainsaw image.

clue.text: Considered millions abandoned and tricked

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: to muse is to ponder or consider
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A businessman who thought about his millions, gave them up, and found he had been conned.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSED loses its M to leave USED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be used is to be exploited or taken advantage of by someone, which is what being tricked amounts to.

clue.text: Mariner who previously played for England

blocks.note: first meaning: a sailor
second meaning: David, the long-serving England goalkeeper

explanation.walkthrough: David Seaman kept goal for Arsenal and England in the 1990s and early 2000s.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an ordinary noun for a sailor and also the surname of a famous former England football goalkeeper.

clue.text: Scandal on Tyneside? Say it's not true

indicators.note: in an across clue one part placed on another comes after it, so the second named part leads

blocks.note: Tyneside is in North East England, abbreviated NE
after Watergate, -gate is tacked onto words to name a scandal

explanation.surface: A local scandal in Newcastle, and someone denying the whole thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle upon Tyne, in North East England.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to deny or contradict a claim, declaring it false.

clue.text: Go on! Bill accompanies one outsider

indicators.note: one part going along with another means the two are set side by side

blocks.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, AD for short
JD Vance, US vice president, one of the political outsiders this puzzle refers to

explanation.surface: An encouraging shout as someone named Bill walks out with a lone misfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's recurring 'outsiders' are the 2025 Trump administration; Vance is its vice president.
explanation.definitionFit: Advance is a command to move forward or proceed, the same urging as telling someone to carry on.

clue.text: Bug 15D on road back

indicators.note: going back means reading the road's name from its end towards its start

blocks.note: the answer to 15 Down sorts things into classes, so another word for it is one who makes lists
the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, London to Edinburgh; the 1 is read as I

explanation.surface: A creepy-crawly from another clue sitting on a road and heading backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is replaced by a synonym of CATEGORIST rather than the answer itself: a lister, then A1 reversed as IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Listeria is a bacterium that causes food poisoning, and a germ is informally called a bug.

clue.text: Locked up auditors' pub - sounded sad

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the words are to be judged by how they sound to the ear

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
to sigh is to make a sad sound

explanation.surface: Accountants in a pub, one of whom gives a mournful sigh.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditors here are hearers, not accountants. INN SIGHED, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside is slang for in prison, as in 'he spent three years inside', so it means locked up.

clue.text: Beware of getting haircut - bloke's uncivilised

definitions.note: a noun phrase: an uncivilised bloke

blocks.note: cave is Latin for beware, old school slang for a lookout's warning
a mane is a long head of hair; cut, it loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A warning about a man who has had a haircut and now behaves like a lout.
explanation.walkthrough: MANE trimmed of its end leaves MAN. Cave (pronounced KAY-vee) was a schoolboy's cry of 'look out!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveman is a prehistoric cave dweller, and figuratively a crude, boorish man without manners.

clue.text: Stop appeal for material

blocks.note: a dam stops water flowing
to appeal for something is to ask

explanation.surface: Calling a halt to a fundraising appeal for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible patterned fabric, often silk or linen, named after the city of Damascus.

clue.text: Figure getting a lot of sex but not as much love on reflection

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes
having not as much means one fewer, so one of the repeated letters is removed
a reflection in a mirror shows things the other way round

blocks.note: nookie is slang for sex
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A celebrity who used to have plenty of sex, reflecting that there is less love in it now.
explanation.walkthrough: NOOKIE loses its last letter (NOOKI), then one O (NOKI), and is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikon is a variant spelling of icon, an image or figure, especially a religious painting of a holy person.

clue.text: God! I'm leaving country

indicators.note: when a country leaves, it departs from the word and its letters are dropped

blocks.note: the setter speaks: Tyrus is the compiler of this puzzle
the United States, US for short

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry from someone emigrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm' stands for the setter's own pseudonym, Tyrus; take away US and the Norse god remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyr is the one-handed Norse war god, whose name survives in the English weekday Tuesday.

clue.text: Fanatical attack involving Britain

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one word holds the other inside

blocks.note: a raid is a sudden attack
B is the abbreviation for Britain or British

explanation.surface: A zealous assault drawing Britain into a conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means extreme and unreasoning in one's views, as of a zealot, by extension from the frenzy of a mad dog.

clue.text: Bill backing FA - outsiders want it

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all, and nada is Spanish for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone supporting the Football Association against a takeover bid by outsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: FA looks like the Football Association, but 'sweet FA' means nothing. The outsiders are the 2025 Trump administration, who spoke of making Canada the 51st US state.
explanation.definitionFit: President Trump repeatedly said the United States should annex its northern neighbour as another state.

clue.text: Cottager is suspect - he works with classified information

indicators.note: something suspect is dodgy and not as it seems, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A villager under suspicion of being a spy handling secret papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' does double duty in the surface but belongs in the fodder; 'classified information' suggests espionage, yet it means data sorted into categories.
explanation.definitionFit: A categorist arranges things into categories, so he literally deals with information that has been classified.

clue.text: Touching gift - not against what one of the outsiders is seeking

definitions.text: what one of the outsiders is seeking

indicators.note: saying not before a word means that word must be taken away from the one before

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
a contribution is something given
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A moving present, given as an alternative to opposing whatever a rogue politician wants.
explanation.walkthrough: CONTRIBUTION without CON leaves TRIBUTION. Trump told supporters in 2023 'I am your retribution', so it is what one outsider seeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Retribution is punishment inflicted as vengeance, which Trump promised to pursue against his political opponents.

clue.text: Going to attend - that's unusual

blocks.note: to go off is to leave, so someone going is off
to attend an event is to be at it

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that it is odd to be going to an event at all.
explanation.walkthrough: BE AT are two separate words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional or eccentric, from music where accents fall on the normally weak beats.

clue.text: Content to share Signal? Leave job

indicators.note: the content of a phrase is what is inside it, so the answer lies within those words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone happy to share messages on the Signal app, then told to quit their post.
explanation.walkthrough: Signal is a messaging app; the 2025 'Signalgate' leak of war plans to a journalist led to calls for officials to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up one's post or job formally, which is exactly leaving a job.

clue.text: Criticise Russian leader before getting a little stressed (are they working on roof?)

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept
a little of the word is just a small piece of it, its first letter
one part going before another means they are joined in that order

blocks.note: to slate is to criticise harshly
first letter of Russian
first letter of stressed

explanation.surface: Someone attacking a Russian leader before he gets slightly stressed, with a puzzled aside about roofers.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaters are tradesmen who lay roofing slates, so they spend their days at work on roofs.

clue.text: Reread by egghead, not BBC man Alan

indicators.note: the letters are read again in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
the head of egg is its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An intellectual goes over a text and declares it is not by a well-known broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like a word for an intellectual, but it splits into egg plus head, the first letter of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Yentob was a long-serving BBC executive and presenter of the arts programme Imagine.

clue.text: Be unbalanced like one on X banning women

indicators.note: banning someone shuts them out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: X is the former Twitter, whose users were tweeters
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A misogynist social-media poster blocking women, and seeming deranged as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: X is Elon Musk's renamed Twitter, fitting the puzzle's theme; TWEETER without W gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to wobble unsteadily, as if about to lose one's balance and fall.

clue.text: Worry new government initiative's pointless

indicators.note: without a point means a compass point letter is taken away

blocks.note: DOGE, the Department of Government Efficiency, set up in 2025
east is a compass point, E

explanation.surface: A grumble that some fresh government scheme is useless and a cause for concern.
explanation.walkthrough: DOGE was the Trump administration's cost-cutting body led by Elon Musk; drop its E.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to trouble or plague them persistently, as worries or misfortunes do.

clue.text: Music's loud! Right about metal ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept
one word placed about another goes round it

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
OK and right both express agreement
last letter of metal

explanation.surface: A complaint that the music is loud, and a correction that it is actually metal.
explanation.walkthrough: OK goes round L, then F leads: F + O(L)K.
explanation.definitionFit: Folk is the genre of traditional music handed down among ordinary people, as opposed to classical or pop.

clue.text: Well-spoken Roman hit man employed by company

indicators.note: someone employed by a firm is taken inside it, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
an icer is one who ices, slang for kills

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking Italian gangster working as a contract killer for the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice is underworld slang for kill, so an icer is a hit man.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was the great orator of the late Roman Republic, the model of eloquent Latin speech.

clue.text: Listener's in spot ignoring outsiders

definitions.note: possessive used as an adjective: of the ear

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters, and ignoring them drops both

blocks.note: to spot something is to notice it

explanation.surface: An eavesdropper concealed in a hiding place, disregarding the people outside.
explanation.walkthrough: NOTICE stripped of its outer letters N and E leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective meaning relating to the ear, the organ a listener uses.

clue.text: Wrong people caught suffering

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so one word is trapped within the other

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are people

explanation.surface: Innocent people arrested by mistake and enduring hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe physical or mental pain, the same as great suffering.

clue.text: Land for sale?

blocks.note: surface reading: a plot of real estate on the market
setter's reading: a country whose name, split in two, is the takeaway phrase for food sold to carry out

explanation.walkthrough: Split the West African country's name as TO GO, an American phrase for takeaway food.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a small West African nation, and its name doubles as the phrase used when buying food to take away.

clue.text: Wrongly seizing woman's old home by force

blocks.note: Ann is a woman's name
an ex is a former partner, so ex means old
being in means being at home
g is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: A woman's former house taken from her by force.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface links to the puzzle's theme of a powerful country wanting another's land.
explanation.definitionFit: Annexing is taking over territory and adding it to one's own, usually without consent, so it is seizing wrongfully.

clue.text: Sudden enlightenment as far as wearing dress

indicators.note: whoever wears a garment is inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a sari is an Indian dress
to means as far as, as in 'up to here'

explanation.surface: A spiritual awakening that comes over someone while dressed in robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Satori is the Zen Buddhist term for a sudden flash of awakening or insight into truth.
